---
title: "Teaching"
---

Currently I teach in three courses at Eindhoven University of Technology: **Behavioural Research Methods 2 (BRM2)**, **Behavioural Research Methods 3 (BRM3)** and **Metascience**.

### Behavioural Research Methods 2 (BRM2):

- Covariate Selection in Multiple Regression: Exploratory vs. Confirmatory Approaches (Coming soon)

- **Introduction to multiple regression**. This lecture
introduces multiple regression analysis, including model specification, interpretation of regression coefficients, model assumptions, and practical applications in R.

<a class="resource-btn" href="https://cristianmesquida.github.io/multiple_regression/">
  <i class="fa-solid fa-book"></i> Book
</a>

- **Introduction to power analysis** (Chapters 1-5). This
lecture covers the principles of statistical power analysis, its role in study design, and how to perform power analyses for common statistical tests using R.

### Behavioural Research Methods 3 (BRM3):

- **P-values and Bayes Factors**. This lecture compares Frequentist and Bayesian approaches to statistical inference. 
Students learn how to interpret *p*-values and Bayes
factors and perform Bayesian analyses for paired and independent-samples *t*-tests.

<a class="resource-btn" href="https://cristianmesquida.github.io/pvalues_and_bayes/slides.pdf">
  <i class="fa-solid fa-person-chalkboard"></i> Slides
</a>

- **Advanced power analysis** (Chapters 6-8). This lecture focuses on power analysis for more advanced study designs,
including equivalence tests using the `TOSTER` package, factorial designs using the
`Superpower` package, and simulation-based approaches in R. 

<div class="resource-links">

<a class="resource-btn" href="https://cristianmesquida.github.io/power_analysis_brm2-3/#/title-slide">
  <i class="fa-solid fa-person-chalkboard"></i> Slides
</a>

<a class="resource-btn" href="https://cristianmesquida.github.io/doing_power_analysis/">
  <i class="fa-solid fa-book"></i> Book
</a>

</div>

- **Equivalence testing**. Equivalence testing. In this lecture, I explain the rationale behind equivalence testing, how it differs from traditional null hypothesis significance testing, and how to conduct and interpret equivalence tests in R using the `TOSTER` package.

<a class="resource-btn" href="https://cristianmesquida.github.io/equivalence_testing/slides.pdf">
  <i class="fa-solid fa-person-chalkboard"></i> Slides
</a>

### Metascience

- **Introduction to meta-analysis**. This lecture introduces the principles of meta-analysis, including effect size estimation, model fitting in R, interpretation of results, and key methodological considerations such as heterogeneity and publication bias.

<a class="resource-btn" href="https://cristianmesquida.github.io/introduction_to_meta-analysis/#/title-slide">
  <i class="fa-solid fa-person-chalkboard"></i> Slides
</a>

- **Bias detection in meta-analysis**. This lecture will cover methods for detecting and assessing bias in meta-analyses, including publication bias, selective reporting, and risk of bias, using R. (Coming soon)
